messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] imputed genotypes
parts:
The red points in plotPXG are the individuals with missing data at the relevant marker, or with incompletely informative genotypes (AB/BB or AA/AB).

You can use pull.geno to grab the genotype data at a marker:

g <- pull.geno(mycross)[,"mymarker"]

and pull.pheno to grab the phenotypes.

Even easier: plotPXG returns the details on the points plotted. It's invisible but you can assign it to something and then look at it.

The output has three columns: the inferred marker genotypes, the phenotypes, and a 0/1 indicator of which genotypes were inferred (0 = not inferred; 1 = inferred)

data(hyper)
out <- plotPXG(hyper, "D1Mit123")
out[1:5,]
table(out[,1], out[,3])
out[ out[,3] == 1, ]

The genotypes (in the first column) are encoded as numbers. For a backcross, 1 = homozygous, 2 = het
For an intercross, 1=AA, 2=AB, 3=BB

karl

parts:
The help files for R functions can be hard to read, and so there's no shame in not having figured this out on your own, but if you take a look at it again (type ?plotPXG), you'll see that it says:

> Value:
>
> A data.frame with initial columns the marker genotypes, then the
> phenotype data, then a column indicating whether any of the marker
> genotypes were inferred (1=at least one genotype inferred, 0=none
> were inferred).

That's trying to say what I said.

The examples in the help files can be the most useful part. Unfortunately, I don't include an example on this feature. I'll look to add such.

karl
